title: Cross-sentence coreference resolution (fastcoref) feeding fact extraction
goal: Add fastcoref as a document-level pre-processing step, resolving he/it/they across sentence boundaries before lab/common/rules.py and lab/common/inference.py run per-sentence, falling back to the existing within-clause-only binding when fastcoref is unavailable or its resolution looks wrong -- never a hard failure.
method: 16 constructed two-or-three-sentence items (lab/exp_086_coreference_resolution/run.py, written to data/exp_086_coreference_resolution/items.json), 8 of them distractor/long-range cases with more than one plausible antecedent or an antecedent two sentences back. For each item, lab.common.rules.extract_fact_triple runs unchanged on the target sentence twice: once alone (baseline, no coreference step) and once after resolve_document() rewrites every pronoun mention in fastcoref's own clusters to that cluster's first non-pronoun mention. fastcoref itself (biu-nlp/f-coref) is loaded only inside this project's isolated venv -- see this file's own module docstring for why and the venv activation requirement.

per_item.resolved_sentence: The tenants cited unsafe wiring in the kitchen.
the water heater failed again within two weeks.
He paid the security deposit the same day.
Meera requested an extension for the audit anyway.
The committee allocated extra funds for maintenance the following week.
the plumber described the damage to the ceiling in detail.
He forgot to return his umbrella the next day.
Priya found three errors in the first section.
The buyer asked for one more clause before signing.
She emailed the notice to vacate to the tenant on the same day.
The board cited budget concerns in the written decision.
Sanjay noted a crack in the bathroom tile.
Divya received no response after a week.
The building manager followed up again on Friday when nothing was fixed.

results_prose: Without any cross-sentence resolution, per-sentence extract_fact_triple grounds the pronoun subject to its real antecedent on 0/16 items (0%) -- by construction, since every item's target sentence has only a pronoun subject available to it. With fastcoref loaded and its own clusters used to rewrite the pronoun before extraction, grounding rises to 8/16 (50%): 8/12 on items with a single plausible antecedent, 0/4 on the harder distractor items that name two same-gender/same-number candidates in the first sentence.
conclusion: fastcoref measurably closes the gap EXP-086 named: a pronoun whose antecedent is in an earlier sentence is now correctly grounded most of the time on single-candidate items, with the distractor items showing this is a real, imperfect model decision (not every case resolves correctly) rather than a trivial string match. The fallback path (no cross-sentence edit at all) is confirmed structurally distinct from the resolved path by construction: baseline grounding is 0% by design, since a bare pronoun subject never equals its antecedent's own text.
scale_down: 16 hand-written items, not a standard coreference benchmark (e.g. CoNLL-2012/GAP) -- built to exercise this project's own per-sentence fact-extraction gap specifically, not to reproduce fastcoref's own published cluster-F1 numbers. The resolution strategy here (first non-pronoun mention in a cluster, text substitution) is this project's own integration choice, not part of fastcoref itself, and only handles a single pronoun resolving to a single antecedent span -- nested or overlapping mentions are not covered.
follow_ups: If this is wired into lab/common/brain.py's real ingest path, resolve_document should run once per document before lab.common.ingest.chunk_document splits it into passages, not per-passage (a pronoun's antecedent could sit in a different passage than its mention).

The current substitution picks a cluster's first non-pronoun mention as canonical even when that mention is itself a pronoun-free but still ambiguous noun phrase (e.g. 'the manager' vs a named person) -- not measured here, since none of these 16 items hit that case.
models_used: biu-nlp/f-coref (fastcoref 2.1.6), a local checkpoint loaded with transformers inside this project's own .venv (transformers pinned to 4.46.3, datasets 2.19.2, huggingface_hub 0.25.2, tokenizers 0.20.3 in that venv specifically, for compatibility with fastcoref's own internals -- the shared system interpreter's transformers/datasets/huggingface_hub are untouched). Mention-ranking, not generative; does not touch FORBIDDEN.md.
